source: U.S. Census Bureau, Survey of Income and Program Participation, 2018-2025 annual public-use files and two-year longitudinal weights; the same people re-interviewed one year apart (2018-2025 panels)
target: Probability that a married, co-resident opposite-sex couple separates or divorces within the next calendar year (the wife reports separated or divorced in any month of the following reference year); prospective
population: U.S. married couples living together in December, wife aged 15+, in SIPP households re-interviewed the next year; the wife’s report and longitudinal weight; reference years 2017-2024
weights: Wife’s two-year longitudinal weight FINYR2 (Census attrition adjustment), normalised to mean 1
timing: All inputs are measured in the baseline year (December or that calendar year), before the outcome year.

inputs.wife_age: wife’s age at the baseline interview
inputs.husband_age: husband’s age at the baseline interview
inputs.marriage_years: years married by December of the baseline year (current marriage); the 2018-2020 files date only first marriages, so it is missing (median-imputed) for remarried people in those years
inputs.wife_education: highest level by December of the baseline year
inputs.wife_earnings: wife’s earnings over the baseline calendar year, dollars (clipped to support)
inputs.husband_earnings: husband’s earnings over the baseline calendar year, dollars
inputs.household_income: household income over the baseline calendar year, dollars
inputs.household_net_worth: household net worth in December of the baseline year, dollars (can be negative)
inputs.household_debt: household total debt in December, dollars
inputs.household_unsecured_debt: household unsecured debt in December, dollars
inputs.children_under18_in_household: number of people under 18 in the household in December (not only the couple’s children)
inputs.wife_months_employed: months with a job in the baseline year (0-12)
inputs.home_owner: Yes/No: home owned or being bought by someone in the household

abstain: same-sex couples (too few in the linked sample)
inputs outside the support (clamp money to it)

models.label: Logistic, both spouses’ demographics and education (spline additive)
Logistic, demographics + earnings, household income, net worth, debt, home ownership, employment, children
Poisson gradient boosting on all inputs (80 trees, depth 2)

models_extended.label: Logistic, demographics + wealth + occupations, husband race-ethnicity, wealth components

heldout.evaluation: train_prospective.py household folds (5), penalty chosen inside each training fold (final C=0.01); paired household bootstrap (1000)

models_extended_note: Held-out comparison of occupation, husband race-ethnicity and wealth components (2026-10-20, extended_predictors.py). Not scored by the app until the form asks for them. Blocks whose held-out difference had a 95% CI above zero: none.

inputs_extended.wife_occupation: wife's job-1 occupation in the baseline December (TJB1_OCC), Census major group, or 'No job'
inputs_extended.husband_race_ethnicity: Hispanic, White, Black, Asian, Other (AIAN, NHPI and multiracial are one residual group in SIPP)
inputs_extended.home_equity: household home equity in December of the baseline year, dollars (clipped to the weighted 1st-99th percentile)
inputs_extended.bank_accounts: household checking, savings and money-market balances, dollars
inputs_extended.stocks_funds: household stocks and mutual funds, dollars
